surface_forms: petite jeune fille, presque encore enfant

appraisal_events.evidence: « Je rentrai, tenant avec désespoir les dix mille francs inespérés » ; « le malheur qu'il engendre annule le bonheur qu'il avait causé » ; « quand le soir venait, j'étais si malheureux que je ne pouvais rester chez moi et allais pleurer dans les bras de femmes que je n'aimais pas » ; « la femme nous cerne de plus en plus, redouble nos chaînes » ; « on les fait plus dures... plus on est vaincu, si toutefois on est en situation de les imposer. Ce n'était pas mon cas à l'égard de Gilberte » ; « je ne voulus plus retourner que rarement chez Mme Swann ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage is organized end to end around the narrator's defeat: the money that was to buy Gilberte's gratitude becomes useless in his hands, his suffering drives him to weep with women he does not love, he withdraws from the Swann house and refuses invitations, and the narration states outright that he is the vanquished party with no standing to impose terms. The closing return of calm is expressly labelled as deceptive and precarious, so it does not reverse the movement.

appraisal_events.evidence: « la personne dont la fausseté récente me faisait encore mal était Gilberte » ; « cette lettre hostile (je n'en reçus qu'une seule qui le fût, de Gilberte) » ; « Gilberte haussant les épaules quand sa mère lui demandait de rester avec moi » ; « Les mots de Gilberte : « Si vous voulez, continuons à lutter » me firent horreur » — mais « l'autre, la réelle, était peut-être entièrement différente de celle-là » et « L'antipathie actuelle de Gilberte pour moi me sembla comme un châtiment infligé par la vie à cause de la conduite que j'avais eue ce jour-là ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator indicts Gilberte for falseness, hostility and contempt, assembling the dream, the one hostile letter, the shrug and the strange laugh into a charge against her. The narration simultaneously undercuts the charge by insisting that the Gilberte he arraigns is a fictive internal figure and by turning the verdict back on his own past conduct, so the blame is staged rather than endorsed.

status_effects.explanation: He loses the happiness his windfall had made possible at the very moment he obtained it, is reduced to nightly weeping and unwanted company, and the text names him explicitly as the beaten party who cannot even set conditions.

Absent and unaware, she nonetheless gains leverage: the passage states as a law applied to his case that each new pain a woman inflicts increases her power and redoubles his chains, and he can no longer be satisfied by the rare meetings that would have contented him the day before.

Her local characterization darkens — falseness, antipathy, the hostile letter, the shrug, the incomprehensible laugh — though the narration flags this portrait as the work of his own suffering imagination.

ambiguities: Gilberte's local direction is genuinely double: the same movement that blackens her character (fausseté, antipathie, hostile letter) is what raises her power over the narrator, and the passage explicitly warns that the Gilberte being judged is an internal fiction (« ma Gilberte fictive »), so the negative appraisal is attributed to the suffering lover rather than confirmed of the real person.

The passage ends with pain subsiding and calm returning (« Le mien finit par revenir »), which could be read as affective recovery; but the text immediately declares that calm « aussi trompeur et précaire qu'avait été le bonheur même » and closes on an irreducible lack, so this is not treated as renewal and does not offset the dominant diminishment.
